name: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarships for College & University Students
provider: Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education (NSP)
summary: Merit-based national scholarship for the top ~20% of Class XII board performers joining regular UG/PG courses, ran through the National Scholarship Portal.

benefit.details: Paid for up to 5 years of the degree including integrated courses; requires 50%+ marks and 75% attendance for renewal.

deadline.label: NSP 2026–27 student deadline (confirmed on the official portal)

special_conditions: Must be above the 80th percentile of the Class XII board — modelled as 80% aggregate
Regular full-time course only; not for distance learning or diploma
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies
Listed by NSP as RENEWAL ONLY for AY 2026–27
Family income up to ₹4.5 lakh and above the 80th percentile in Class XII

steps: Register on scholarships.gov.in (fresh registration)
Select 'Central Sector Scheme' under Department of Higher Education
Fill academic and bank details, upload documents
Complete institute and board verification
Monitor NSP dashboard for payment

notes: RENEWAL ONLY for AY 2026–27. The official NSP announcement names PM-USP CSSS explicitly as open for renewal applications, closing 31-10-2026, with institute verification to 15-11-2026 and Level-2 verification to 30-11-2026. Fresh applicants should check the NSP dashboard before assuming a fresh window exists.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Students from Minority Communities
summary: Central post-matric scholarship for students of six notified minority communities studying Class XI to PhD with family income within ₹2 lakh.

benefit.details: Maintenance allowance (hosteller/day scholar) plus course fee reimbursement subject to limits.

special_conditions: 30% of scholarships earmarked for girl students
State domicile applies — apply under your home state quota

steps: Register on NSP and choose Ministry of Minority Affairs schemes
Score ≥50% in the last exam: upload marksheet
Provide community and income proofs
Complete institute verification

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities
provider: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (NSP)
summary: Central scholarship for students with 40%+ benchmark disability from Class XI onwards, including maintenance, disability allowance and fee support.

benefit.details: Maintenance allowance + disability allowance + book allowance; hosteller rates higher.

special_conditions: Benchmark disability = 40% or more with valid UDID/disability certificate
50% reservation for girl candidates — unfilled seats transferable
UDID portal registration and consent to share UDID details is MANDATORY before submitting the NSP application — without it the application cannot be submitted at all (NSP announcement, AY 2026–27)

steps: Register on NSP under Department of Empowerment of PwD
Upload UDID and income certificate
Complete institute verification
Track application until DBT

notes: UDID consent is now a hard prerequisite — NSP will not accept the application without it. Register on the UDID portal first and allow time for the certificate, because it is issued separately and is not instant.

name: Merit Cum Means Scholarship for Professional & Technical Courses (CS)
summary: For minority-community students in professional/technical UG & PG courses (engineering, medicine, management, law, CA etc.) with income up to ₹2.5 lakh.

benefit.details: Course fee reimbursement up to ₹20,000 + maintenance allowance (hosteller/day scholar).

special_conditions: Only professional/technical courses on the approved list (85 listed courses)
Admission through a competitive entrance exam or 50% in qualifying exam

steps: Register on NSP → Ministry of Minority Affairs
Select Merit Cum Means and verify course is on approved list
Upload proofs and complete institute verification
Renew annually with 50%+ marks

name: Top Class Education Scheme for SC Students
summary: Premier-institute scholarship for SC students admitted to notified 'top class' institutions (IITs, NITs, AIIMS, NLUs etc.) — full tuition plus living and device allowances.

benefit.details: Full tuition waived/deposited + ₹86,000 living & other allowances in the first year incl. laptop/books, ~₹41,000 for later years.

special_conditions: Institution must be on the notified Top Class institution list
Income cap revised in recent cycles (₹3.5 lakh) — verify current order
All SC students of the institution within income limit are covered (no slot lottery)

documents: Admission proof in a Top Class institution

steps: Register on NSP → Ministry of Social Justice
Confirm your institution is on the notified list
Upload SC + income proofs and submit
Institute forwards to the Ministry for sanction

name: Begum Hazrat Mahal National Scholarship
provider: Maulana Azad Education Foundation, Ministry of Minority Affairs
summary: National scholarship for meritorious girl students of minority communities studying in Class IX–XII.

benefit.details: One-time annual assistance credited via DBT.

special_conditions: Girl students of minority communities only
50%+ marks in the last exam required

steps: Register on the scholarship portal when the cycle opens
Fill personal, school and bank details
Upload proofs and submit
Verify selection status on the portal

notes: Portal/schedule seen to shift between years — re-verify when the cycle opens.

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girls (Technical Education)
provider: All India Council for Technical Education
summary: ₹50,000/year for girl students admitted to AICTE-approved UG degree or diploma programmes via centralised admission.

benefit.details: Lump-sum annual amount for fees, books, equipment and contingencies; duration of the programme.

special_conditions: Admission to an AICTE-approved technical programme in the first year (or lateral entry)
Maximum two girl children per family
Merit of the qualifying admission exam decides selection — 10,000 seats/year

steps: Register on NSP → AICTE schemes
Select Pragati and enter institute AISHE details
Upload admission + income proofs
Institute verifies; renewal each year on promotion

name: AICTE Saksham Scholarship (Students with Disability, Technical Education)
provider: All India Council for Technical Education
summary: ₹50,000/year for students with 40%+ disability admitted to AICTE-approved technical degree or diploma programmes.

benefit.details: Lump sum towards academic expenses for the programme duration.

special_conditions: Disability of 40%+ certified as per RPwD Act
First-year (or lateral entry) admission in AICTE-approved course required
UDID portal registration and consent to share UDID details is MANDATORY before submitting the NSP application — without it the application cannot be submitted at all (NSP announcement, AY 2026–27)

steps: Register on NSP → AICTE → Saksham
Upload disability and admission proofs
Complete institute verification
Renew annually on successful promotion

name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship (NMMS)
provider: Department of School Education & Literacy, Ministry of Education
summary: Arrests school drop-out after Class VIII: ₹12,000/year for talented students from low-income families from Class IX to XII.

benefit.details: For Classes IX–XII in government/government-aided/local-body schools; state NMMS exam selects awardees.

deadline.label: NSP 2026–27 student deadline, EXTENDED from 31 Aug → 30 Sep → 31 Oct 2026

special_conditions: Selection through the State NMMS examination (MAT + SAT) in Class VIII
Continuation in Class IX–XII requires qualifying the NMMS exam
55%+ in Class VII (50% for reserved categories) — modelled as 55%

steps: Apply for the state NMMS exam via SCERT in Class VIII
Clear MAT & SAT cut-offs fixed by the state
Open the NSP application within the national window
Get school + district verification for disbursement

notes: Two different dates are easily confused here. The state NMMS SELECTION EXAM (MAT + SAT) for Class VIII students is held around Nov–Dec 2026 (e.g. Delhi 5 Dec, Odisha 6 Dec) and is run by each SCERT. The NSP SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION for students who already qualify closed 31 October 2026, after the Ministry of Education extended it twice. Institute (L1) verification ran to 15 Nov and district (L2) to 30 Nov 2026. 88,522 fresh and 1,97,133 renewal applications had been filed by 30 Sep 2026.

name: Ishan Uday Special Scholarship Scheme (North Eastern Region, UGC)
summary: UGC's scholarship for students domiciled in the eight North-Eastern states pursuing the first year of a general/professional/technical/medical/paramedical degree course anywhere in India.

benefit.details: Monthly scholarship for the full duration of the first degree course (10 months/year).

special_conditions: Domicile of one of the eight NER states
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies
Admission within the notified time after +2

documents: Domicile certificate of the NER state
Admission proof of the first-year UG course

steps: Register on NSP
Choose Ishan Uday (UGC schemes)
Upload documents
Institute verification -> DBT

notes: UGC opened the 2026–27 window late, on 16 September 2026, well after the portal's general 1 June opening. 10,000 fresh awards a year for first-year UG students domiciled in a North Eastern state. Apply on NSP — ugc.gov.in does not take the application.

name: National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies (NSPGS)
provider: University Grants Commission (UGC), Ministry of Education — via NSP
summary: The umbrella PG merit scholarship, ₹15,000 a month for 10 months over two years, for 10,000 students a year. It replaced four separate UGC PG schemes — Indira Gandhi Single Girl Child, University Rank Holders, SC/ST Professional Courses, and GATE/GPAT — so there is now ONE application for all of them.

benefit.amount_display: ₹15,000 / month for 10 months (₹1.5 lakh / year, 2 years)
benefit.details: Disbursed by UGC through DBT to an Aadhaar-seeded account. Renewal for the second year requires a separate NSP renewal application plus successful completion of the first year — the second year is NOT processed automatically.

special_conditions: First PG degree only — anyone who has ALREADY acquired a postgraduate degree is not eligible
Under 30 years of age as on the date of admission to the first semester/year of the PG programme
Regular, full-time mode only — open, distance and private mode are excluded
No income ceiling at all; selection is purely on merit

30% of slots reserved for women candidates, with preference given to single girl children (a single girl child is the only girl in the family with no brothers or sisters; one of twin or fraternal daughters also qualifies)
50% of slots for Arts, Humanities, Social Sciences, Law and Management; 50% for Science, Engineering & Technology, Medical, Technical, Agriculture and Forestry
10,000 slots per annum, allocated per the Government of India reservation policy
Applications are invited once a year, only on NSP
The institution must hold a valid AISHE code
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
UG marksheet and degree / provisional certificate
Single-girl-child affidavit, if claiming that preference

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'National Scholarship for Post Graduate Studies' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: If you were told to apply for the 'Indira Gandhi Single Girl Child Scholarship' or the 'PG Scholarship for University Rank Holders', those no longer exist as separate schemes — both were merged into NSPGS, whose official FAQ is linked above. Verify the exact opening and closing dates on your NSP dashboard, because UGC schemes opened later (16 Sep) than the portal generally (1 Jun) and the FAQ itself says deadlines are displayed on NSP rather than fixed in the guideline.

name: PM YASASVI Central Sector Scheme of Top Class Education in College (OBC / EBC / DNT)
provider: Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (Backward Classes), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
summary: Merit-cum-means scholarship for OBC, EBC and Denotified-Nomadic-Semi-Nomadic Tribe students studying at college level, covering tuition up to ₹2 lakh a year plus a maintenance allowance.

benefit.amount_display: Full tuition up to ₹2,00,000 / year + maintenance allowance
benefit.details: Tuition is reimbursed at actuals up to the ceiling; the maintenance allowance is paid in addition for hostellers and day scholars at different rates.

special_conditions: For OBC, Economically Backward Classes (EBC) and DNT / SNT (Denotified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribe) students
EBC and DNT applicants are covered under the 'general' category in FeeFix — check the scheme's own certificate requirements, which differ from a standard OBC certificate
Admission in a recognised college / university, regular mode
Selected through the PM YASASVI entrance test for the school component; the college component is merit-cum-means on the qualifying examination
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
OBC / EBC / DNT caste or community certificate
Fee receipt or fee structure from the institute

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'PM YASASVI Top Class Education in College' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: The SCHOOL-level component of PM YASASVI (Classes IX–XII) is a separate listing and was reported as RENEWAL ONLY for 2026–27 with an earlier closing date; the college component is open for fresh applicants. Confirm which one applies to you on the NSP dashboard before relying on this deadline.

name: AICTE Swanath Scholarship Scheme (Technical Degree & Diploma)
provider: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) — via NSP
summary: ₹50,000 a year for students in AICTE-approved degree or diploma programmes who have lost one or both parents, and for wards of defence and paramilitary personnel martyred in action.

benefit.details: A lump-sum grant towards tuition, books, equipment and software — not a maintenance allowance. Paid for the full duration of the degree or diploma.

special_conditions: Student is a ward of a parent (or both parents) deceased, OR a ward of defence / paramilitary personnel martyred in action
Admission in an AICTE-approved degree or diploma programme
One award per family per year
Listed by NSP as a WELFARE-based scheme, so it can be held alongside one merit-based scheme from AY 2026–27

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
Death certificate of the parent(s), or
Martyrdom certificate from the defence / paramilitary authority

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'AICTE Swanath Scholarship Scheme' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: Distinct from AICTE Pragati (girl students) and AICTE Saksham (specially-abled students), which are separate NSP listings. A student can only hold one AICTE award, but because Swanath is welfare-based it may be combined with one merit-based scheme from AY 2026–27.

name: PM USP Special Scholarship Scheme for Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh
provider: Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education) — via NSP
summary: Merit-based scholarship for students domiciled in Jammu & Kashmir or Ladakh, covering up to ₹3 lakh a year including medical courses, on the NSP portal.

benefit.details: Covers tuition and a maintenance allowance; the ceiling is highest for medical and other professional programmes.

deadline.label: NSP 2026–27 student deadline — RENEWAL ONLY, confirmed on the official portal

special_conditions: Domicile of Jammu & Kashmir or Ladakh is mandatory
RENEWAL ONLY for AY 2026–27 — the official NSP announcement names this scheme explicitly as open for renewal applications
Studying in a professional / technical degree programme in India
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'PM USP Special Scholarship Scheme For Jammu Kashmir And Ladakh' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: Verified directly against the NSP Announcements page, which states: 'Renewal applications for the PM-USP – CSSS and PM USP Special Scholarship Scheme For Jammu Kashmir And Ladakh is currently open in NSP. Closing dates for student application is 31-10-2026 and closing date for institute verification is 15-11-2026 and closing date for L2 verification is 30/11/2026.' First-year students should not assume a fresh window is open.

name: National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students
provider: Ministry of Tribal Affairs — via NSP
summary: Replaced the earlier 'Top Class Education for ST Students' scheme. Supports ST students from Class IX onward through higher education and research fellowships, up to ₹2.5 lakh a year.

benefit.details: Tiered by course level: school, higher secondary, UG/PG and professional courses each carry a different ceiling, with the highest for professional and research programmes.

special_conditions: ST category certificate is mandatory
Formerly listed on NSP as 'Top Class Education for ST Students' — the scheme was renamed and widened to include a fellowship component for research students
Admission in a recognised institution, regular mode
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
Admission letter and fee structure of the institute

application.portal: National Scholarship Portal (Ministry of Tribal Affairs)
steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education of ST Students' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: Marked pending_review: the scheme's existence and its replacement of 'Top Class Education for ST Students' is confirmed by multiple NSP scheme listings for 2026–27, but the exact income ceiling and tier-wise amounts should be confirmed against the Ministry of Tribal Affairs guideline before relying on them. The 31 Oct 2026 deadline follows the common NSP 2026–27 student deadline.

name: Free Coaching for SCs, OBCs and Beneficiaries of the PM Cares Children Scheme
provider: Department of Social Justice & Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
summary: Fully funded coaching for competitive and entrance examinations — civil services, engineering, medical, law, management and other professional courses — at empanelled institutes.

benefit.amount_display: Coaching fee paid in full, plus hostel and mess charges
benefit.details: Not a cash scholarship. The ministry pays the empanelled coaching institute directly and covers hostel/mess where the student is resident. amount_annual_inr is 0 because no cash reaches the student.

deadline.label: NSP 2026–27 student deadline (this scheme opened later, on 03-08-2026)

special_conditions: SC or OBC candidates, OR beneficiaries of the PM Cares Children Scheme — the PM Cares group is why 'general' is listed as an eligible category in FeeFix
Coaching is delivered only at institutes empanelled by the ministry; the choice of institute is limited to that list
Listed by NSP as a WELFARE-based scheme, so it may be held alongside one merit-based scheme from AY 2026–27
A student may avail free coaching for a maximum of two attempt-cycles under the scheme

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
SC / OBC caste certificate, or PM Cares Children Scheme sanction letter
Proof of the target examination / course being applied for

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'Free Coaching For SCs, OBCs And Beneficiaries Of PM Cares Children Scheme' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: Opened on 3 August 2026, two months after the portal's general 1 June opening, but shares the common 31 October 2026 student deadline. This is coaching, not cash — a student expecting a credit in their bank account will be disappointed; the benefit is a seat at an empanelled institute.

name: Scholarship for Top-Class Education for Students with Disabilities
provider: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
summary: Full tuition support plus maintenance for students with benchmark disabilities (40% or more) studying at notified top-class institutions.

benefit.amount_display: Full tuition + maintenance, up to ~₹1,40,000 / year
benefit.details: Covers tuition at actuals, a maintenance allowance, and support for books, equipment and, where applicable, a course-access allowance.

special_conditions: Benchmark disability — 40% or more — certified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
Admission at a notified top-class institution (IITs, IIMs, AIIMS, NITs, central universities and others on the ministry's notified list)
UDID portal registration and consent to share UDID details is MANDATORY before submitting the NSP application — without it the application cannot be submitted at all (NSP announcement, AY 2026–27)
Separate from the Post-Matric Scholarship for Students with Disabilities, which is not restricted to notified institutions
From AY 2026–27 a student may hold ONE merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes, per each scheme's eligibility — the older 'one scholarship only' restriction no longer applies

documents: Aadhaar (for OTR generation and DBT seeding)
Income certificate (issued by the competent authority)
Category certificate, where the scheme requires one
Bonafide / admission certificate from the institute
UDID card (mandatory — generate it before applying)
Disability certificate showing 40% or more benchmark disability
Admission letter from a notified top-class institution

steps: Generate your One Time Registration (OTR) on NSP using Aadhaar or your Aadhaar enrolment ID — OTR is required for every NSP scheme from AY 2024–25
Log in to scholarships.gov.in with your OTR
Select 'Scholarship for Top-Class Education for Students with Disabilities' from the scheme list
Select the scheme and fill academic, personal and bank details
Upload the required documents
Submit before the student deadline, then follow up with your institute for Level-1 (INO) verification
Track Level-2 (district/state) verification on the NSP dashboard

notes: The UDID requirement is new for AY 2026–27 and is a hard blocker: NSP states that disabled students who have not logged into the UDID portal and consented to share their UDID details 'will not be able to submit their application'. UDID certification is a separate process with its own waiting time, so start it well before the deadline.
